name: Put: Sixteen Hands
summary: A two-player trick-taking bluffing duel over 16 hands. After the first trick, each player may secretly call Put to raise the stake from 1 to 4, and a lone Put can be seen or folded to.

player.meaning: The player's unplayed cards, as values 1-13
Card played face up to trick 1 (0 = none yet)
Card auto-played to trick 2, the higher of the two remaining
Card auto-played to trick 3, the last card
Put or Check, chosen secretly in the put window and announced after
See or Fold, given only by the lone Checker when exactly one player Put

game.meaning: The undealt cards: four copies of each value 1-13
Number of the current hand, 1 to 16
Seat that leads this hand: 1 in odd hands, 2 in even hands
Points the hand is worth: 4 if a Put was seen, 1 if both Checked
True if the lone Checker folded this hand

setup: Both players' score is set to 0.
The match will last exactly 16 hands.

round.effect: Reset step. hand_number += 1. leader = 1 if hand_number is odd, else 2. deck = four copies of each value 1..13 (52 cards). Each player's hand, card1, card2 and card3 are cleared to empty or 0, call and response to empty text, and tricks to 0. stake = 0 and folded = false.
Deal step. Each player draws 3 cards at random: each card is removed from deck and appended to that player's hand.
Each player privately sees their own hand.

round.answer: one card value from their hand
round.effect: Lead step. leader.card1 = the chosen value; one copy of that value is removed from leader.hand.

round.who: the responder (the seat that is not leader)
round.answer: one card value from their hand
round.effect: Answer step. responder.card1 = the chosen value; one copy of that value is removed from responder.hand.

Trick 1. If seat1.card1 > seat2.card1, seat1.tricks += 1. If seat2.card1 > seat1.card1, seat2.tricks += 1. If the cards are equal, the trick is a tie and no one's tricks change. The result is announced.
Put window. Each player's call is set to their answer. Neither player sees the other's call until both have answered.

round.who: the player whose call is Check, only when exactly one player's call is Put
round.effect: Reply step. That player's response is set to the answer. When both called Put or both called Check, this step is skipped.

Stake step. If both calls are Put, or one call is Put and the Checker's response is See, then stake = 4. If both calls are Check, then stake = 1. If the Checker's response is Fold, then folded = true.
Fold scoring, only when folded is true. The player whose call is Put gets score += 1. The remaining cards are not shown.

Trick 2, only when folded is false. Each player's card2 = the maximum value in their hand, and that card is removed from hand. Compare card2: the higher card gives its owner tricks += 1; equal cards are a tie.
Trick 3, only when folded is false. Each player's card3 = their last card in hand, and hand becomes empty. Compare card3: the higher card gives its owner tricks += 1; equal cards are a tie.
Reveal, only when folded is false. Announce each seat's card1, card2 and card3 and each seat's tricks.
Hand scoring, only when folded is false. A player with tricks >= 2 gets score += stake. If neither player has tricks >= 2, no one scores.
End check. If hand_number >= 16, end the match; otherwise the next hand begins.

ending.decided_by: After 16 hands, the player with the higher total score wins. Equal totals share the win, which is a draw.

rules.text: When a hand begins, then the deck is restored to 52 cards, four copies of each value 1 to 13, and each player's hand, played cards, call, response and tricks are cleared, along with stake and folded.
When cards are dealt, then each player receives 3 cards drawn from the deck, and each player sees only their own cards.
When hand_number is odd, then seat 1 leads; when hand_number is even, then seat 2 leads.
When the leader leads, then they play one card from their own hand face up, and it is announced before the responder plays.
When the responder answers, then they play one card from their own hand face up, having seen the lead.
When a trick is compared, then the higher value wins the trick and adds 1 to its owner's tricks; when the values are equal, then the trick is a tie and no one's tricks change.
When the put window opens, then both players choose Put or Check simultaneously, without seeing the other's choice, and both calls are then announced.
When exactly one player calls Put, then the player who called Check chooses See or Fold.
When both players call Put, or one calls Put and the other Sees, then stake = 4.
When both players call Check, then there is no Put, no reply is asked, and stake = 1.
When the Checker folds, then the player who called Put scores 1 point, no further tricks are played, and the remaining cards are not shown.
When no one folded, then in trick 2 each player automatically plays the higher of their two remaining cards.
When no one folded, then in trick 3 each player automatically plays their last card.
When no one folded, then after trick 3 all cards and each player's tricks are revealed.
When no one folded and a player has won at least 2 of the 3 tricks, then that player's score increases by the stake, 1 or 4.
When no one folded and neither player has won 2 tricks because of tied tricks, then no one scores that hand.
When hand 16 has been scored, then the match ends, and the higher total score wins; equal totals are a draw.

offers.question: Lead: which card to play
offers.who: the leader (seat 1 in odd hands, seat 2 in even hands)
offers.options: each distinct card value in the leader's 3-card hand

offers.question: Answer: which card to play
offers.options: each distinct card value in the responder's 3-card hand

offers.question: Reply to a lone Put
offers.who: only the seat that called Check, and only when the other seat called Put

choices.why: The designer fixed the table at 2. The game is a heads-up duel: three tricks between two hands and a Put that one opponent sees or folds to. It has no meaning at another size. The strategy is reading the opponent's lead and answer from trick 1, putting to bluff or value-bet, and folding a weak hand for a 1-point loss rather than risking 4.
The source says there is no talk phase.

choices.what: Cards are stored as numbers 1-13 rather than named ranks
choices.why: Arithmetic comparison needs numbers; the rank names map one to one (13 = Three, highest, down to 1 = Four, lowest), so nothing is lost.

choices.what: Played cards and calls are public attributes
choices.why: The rules play them face up or announce them.

choices.what: The fold scores the fixed 1 point (fold_points), not the stake
choices.why: The source says the Putter scores 1 point when the other folds.

simplifications.what: Steps that apply only in some situations (reply, fold scoring, tricks 2 and 3, reveal, hand scoring) are single steps, each carrying its own arithmetic condition
simplifications.why: The step list is flat. Each skipped step depends on one simple condition (folded, or exactly one Put), so no block of steps has to be chosen instead of another.
